trĭcămĕrātus , a, um, adj. tres-camera,
I.having three chambers (late Lat.). ecclesia, Aug. Civ. Dei, 15, 26: inferiora ar cae bicamerata et tricamerata facies, Ambros. Hexaëm. 6, 9, n. 72.—Subst.: trĭcă-mĕrātum , i, n., a room divided into three chambers, Hier. adv. Jovin. 1, 17.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
